column2: Clearly state what students are expected to learn, know, or be able to do by the end of the lesson. This should align with curriculum goals and focus on the knowledge, skill, or understanding being developed.

Describe how students will know they have successfully achieved the learning intention. Include specific, observable, and measurable indicators of success that help guide student self-assessment and teacher feedback.
Write these using "I can" statements

Outline how you will engage students at the start of the lesson. This could be a question, activity, story, image, or challenge that sparks curiosity and connects to students’ prior knowledge or interests.

Detail the direct instruction or guided learning that introduces and models the core content or skill. Include key explanations, demonstrations, strategies, or tools used to support student understanding.

Describe the main activity or set of activities students will complete to apply and practice what they’ve learned. Tasks should be purposeful, aligned with the learning intention, and allow for formative assessment.

Explain how students will reflect on their learning at the end of the lesson. This could include self-assessment, class discussion, journaling, or sharing. Reflection should help consolidate learning and connect to the success criteria.

Specify how the lesson will be adapted to meet the diverse learning needs of students. Include strategies for supporting different readiness levels, learning styles, interests, or specific learning needs (e.g., scaffolds, extensions, choice).
